name: Fortinet FortiGate — Web C2 Beacon (Recurring Uncommon-Domain Callbacks) [host/user-scoped]
xql_query:
dataset = fortinet_fortigate_raw
| filter act = "accept" and FTNTFGTsubtype = "forward"
| filter requestClientApplication != null and requestClientApplication not contains "Mozilla"
| filter src != null and suser != null and dhost != null
| comp count() as beacon_count by suser, src, dhost, shost
| filter beacon_count >= 8
| alter user_name = suser, int_host = src, url = dhost, host_name = shost
description: Repeated Accepted outbound forward-traffic sessions from one internal host/user through the FortiGate to a single domain using a NON-BROWSER HTTP client (Go/python/curl/scanner user-agents, i.e. requestClientApplication that is not a Mozilla browser string) — the perimeter-firewall signature of a scripted HTTP C2 beacon. Deliberately HOST/USER-SCOPED: it carries suser (the exact box user) and the internal client IP as alert entities so XSIAM attributes the alert to the same asset/user the Cortex endpoint alerts are keyed on, letting endpoint + network fold into one case. FortiGate does not tag an Uncategorized web-reputation on forward traffic the way the other NGFWs do, so the non-browser user-agent is the discriminator that keeps ambient browsing out.
alert_name: Fortinet FortiGate — Web C2 Beacon (Recurring Uncommon-Domain Callbacks)
alert_description:
What fired: >=8 Accepted outbound sessions from one internal host/user through the FortiGate to a single domain, all using a non-browser HTTP client (Go/python/curl-class user-agent) within the search window — a low-and-slow scripted HTTP C2 beacon.

Why it matters: a host is beaconing to external web infrastructure at a regular cadence with a scripted (non-browser) client — classic automated C2 check-in. Assessed severity: High.

MITRE ATT&CK: T1071.001 - Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols (TA0011 - Command and Control).

Investigate:
  - Identify the internal client (host_name/int_host) and user (user_name) and the beaconed domain (url); check domain reputation, registration age, and resolution history.
  - Pivot to the endpoint on the same host/user for the process behind the non-browser client (correlate with Cortex agent alerts on that asset).
  - Confirm the destination is not an expected/authorized automation endpoint before escalating.
